title: Relative Mayer Vietoris for qcqs etale compact support
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. All derived categories below are the bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For a separated finite-type morphism $h:T\to B$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and a compactification $c=(j:T\hookrightarrow\overline T,p:\overline T\to B)$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper, set $Rh_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes and let $U,V\subset X$ be quasi-compact opens with $X=U\cup V$. Put $a=f|_U$, $b=f|_V$, $d=f|_{U\cap V}$. For $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and any chosen compactifications for $a,b,d,f$, there is a distinguished triangle $Rd_!(K|_{U\cap V})\to Ra_!(K|_U)\oplus Rb_!(K|_V)\to Rf_!K\to Rd_!(K|_{U\cap V})[1]$, where each shriek denotes its chosen candidate.

source.place: Tag 0GKN, label lemma-relative-mayer-vietoris; finite-ring bounded-below specialization

proof.text: Put $W=U\cap V$ and write $k_T:T\hookrightarrow X$ for $T=U,V,W$. The affine-intersection criterion [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion] shows that opens of $X$ are quasi-separated. Choose finite affine covers of $U$ and $V$; the intersections of their members are quasi-compact by the same criterion, so their finite union $W$ is quasi-compact. Thus all three sources are qcqs. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], each $k_T$ is quasi-compact. An open immersion is locally of finite type: inside an affine neighbourhood, principal opens contained in the open subscheme have coordinate ring $A[t]/(at-1)$. It is separated since its diagonal is an isomorphism. The same principal-open calculation applied to affine finite-type presentations for $f$ proves that $fk_T$ is locally of finite type; it is quasi-compact by the cited permanence lemma (source qc, target qs), hence finite type. Its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $f$, hence closed. Therefore composition may be applied to $k_T,f$.

source.place: Tag 0GKN, label lemma-relative-mayer-vietoris, hypotheses for open inclusions

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-constant-ring-module-equivalence] to identify sheaves valued in $\Lambda$-modules, used in the extension-by-zero definition, with sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $\Lambda_X$, used in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. This equivalence keeps the underlying abelian presheaves and their maps unchanged and is exact. Restriction and the sheafification defining extension by zero agree under it: restrict the scalar action to constant sections, or extend it uniquely along the constant-ring sheafification map. Thus the following maps and exact sequences are in the coefficient category of the statement. For a sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$, form $A(F)=k_{W!}(F|_W)$ and $B(F)=k_{U!}(F|_U)\oplus k_{V!}(F|_V)$. For $T=U,V$, on any etale object $E\to W$ the extension-by-zero presheaf for $k_T$ has value $F(E)$, since $E\to X$ factors through $T$. Its sheafification restricted to $W$ is therefore $F|_W$: covers of an object over $W$ remain over $W$, and $F|_W$ is already a sheaf. Thus $k_W^{-1}k_{T!}(F|_T)=F|_W$. Under [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], the identity of $F|_W$ now defines $A(F)\to k_{T!}(F|_T)$. Take the negative of this map for $T=V$; define $B(F)\to F$ by the two counits. Their composite is zero, since the two composites $A(F)\to F$ both correspond to $\mathrm{id}_{F|_W}$. The stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks], including its explicit map on germs, and the explicit counits in the adjunction identify the stalk sequence at a point in $W$ with $0\to M\xrightarrow{(1,-1)}M\oplus M\xrightarrow{(1,1)}M\to0$, where $M=F_{\bar x}$. At a point of $U\setminus V$ or $V\setminus U$ it is $0\to0\to M\xrightarrow{1}M\to0$. These exhaust the points since $U\cup V=X$. All three sequences are exact. To justify detection, forget scalars using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]; exact stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] make the kernel, middle homology and cokernel have zero stalks. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to each of their maps to zero. Faithfulness of forgetting scalars implies that a module with zero underlying sheaf is zero. Thus $0\to A(F)\to B(F)\to F\to0$ is short exact in module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0GKK, label lemma-mayer-vietoris-shriek, stalk calculation in its proof

proof.text: Represent $K$ by a bounded-below complex $L$. Restriction is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and extension by zero is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], so their termwise operations represent $K|_T$ and $k_{T!}(K|_T)$ and preserve a common lower bound. Naturality of the maps in step 2 makes its sequences in degrees $L^n$ a short exact sequence of complexes $0\to A(L)\to B(L)\to L\to0$. The module category is abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to obtain the distinguished triangle $k_{W!}K|_W\to k_{U!}K|_U\oplus k_{V!}K|_V\to K\to(k_{W!}K|_W)[1]$. All its objects lie in $D^+$; the same mapping-cone construction gives the bounded-below triangle.

source.place: Tag 0GKK, label lemma-mayer-vietoris-shriek; Tag 0152, label lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor

proof.text: Fix the compactification $(j,p)$ chosen for $f$. The functor $j_!$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], hence its termwise derived functor is triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. The module categories on $\overline X$ and $Y$ are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian] and have K-injective resolutions by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence]. The module direct image $p_*$ is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact]. Apply [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] to $p_*$: $Rp_*$ preserves distinguished triangles and commutes with shifts. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] it preserves bounded-below objects; $j_!$ also does so termwise. Thus $Rf_!^{(j,p)}=Rp_*j_!$ is triangulated on $D^+$. Apply it to step 3. Additivity identifies the middle vertex with $Rf_!k_{U!}K|_U\oplus Rf_!k_{V!}K|_V$, and shift compatibility identifies the last vertex with $(Rf_!k_{W!}K|_W)[1]$.

source.place: Tag 0GKN, label lemma-relative-mayer-vietoris, applying the triangulated compact-support functor; Tag 0159, label lemma-right-derived-properties

proof.text: For each $T=U,V,W$, choose the compactification $(k_T,1_X)$ of $k_T$. Here $1_X$ is proper (its diagonal is an isomorphism, its affine presentation is the identity, and every base change is an identity closed map). By [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification], $R(k_T)_!^{(k_T,1_X)}=R(1_X)_*k_{T!}=k_{T!}$: identity direct image is the identity, and applying it to a resolution gives the same object in the derived category. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-qcqs-composition] to $T\xrightarrow{k_T}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$, choosing for the composite exactly the compactification specified in the statement for $a,b,d$. This gives natural isomorphisms $Rf_!k_{U!}\cong Ra_!$, $Rf_!k_{V!}\cong Rb_!$, $Rf_!k_{W!}\cong Rd_!$. Let their evaluations on the restricted complexes be $e_U,e_V,e_W$. The isomorphism on the middle vertex is $e_U\oplus e_V$, on the third vertex the identity, and on the last vertex $e_W[1]$. If the arrows of the triangle in step 4 are $u,v,w$, define the new arrows by $(e_U\oplus e_V)u e_W^{-1}$, $v(e_U\oplus e_V)^{-1}$, and $e_W[1]w$. These formulas give an isomorphism of triangles, so the resulting triangle is distinguished and is exactly the triangle asserted for the chosen candidates.
